Emphatic stress is the placement of greater stress on a particular word or syllable in an utterance. This is done for emphasis or clarification. In this case, emphatic stress is placed on "staying" in the utterance to clarify an error that was made in the question. This means that the question that should be selected should be one that contains a word or phrase that contrasts with "staying" while everything else remains the same. This is why "Is Musa going through Enugu" is the answer to this question.

Is Musa going through Enugu?

No. Musa is STAYING in Enugu.

options.text: Is Musa staying on the outskirt of Enugu?

26806.subject: English Language
26806.question_text: It can be deduced from the passage that snakes have
26806.explanation:
The passage states:

"Many snakes have specialized jaws that enable them to swallow animals that are far larger than their own heads."

This means snakes attempt to swallow prey much larger than their heads. From this, we can deduce that snakes do not judge the size of prey visually in the same way humans do. They lack an effective visual sense of measurement. If they accurately measured size by sight, they would be less likely to attempt swallowing prey that appears impossibly large.

While the passage says:

"Some snakes, such as the African rock python, have been observed eating animals as large as an antelope or a small cow."

This does not mean snakes have a special appetite for antelopes. It simply gives an example of the largest prey some snakes can consume.
